scope: HOSTED round for the three newest servers - quotes (Extension 7), calendar and pdf (Extension 4) - through the URL-token endpoints https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/<server>/t/<token> as a claude.ai user arrives. Eighteen prompts, six per server, adapted from Part 2 of docs/QUOTES_AUDIT.md, docs/CALENDAR_AUDIT.md and docs/PDF_AUDIT.md, with the two things only the hosted path forces: two PDFs pasted as base64 through pdf_upload, and an .ics pasted as text because ics_import path is refused by design and ics_import url is Pro, so paste is the whole free path. Free tier, one fresh anonymous token, one seed (invoice business_set by curl) so the quotes lane had a business identity the way the local Part 2 did.
method: One anonymous token minted with GET https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/connect (anon_9018420e8c11890e1671d0ea5ca1887e) and reused for every lane. Registered PER LANE only, because the free tier is 600 calls per hour per token and a CLI session re-handshakes every registered endpoint on every turn (D-R53): quotes+invoice, calendar+timezone, pdf alone. Client: claude CLI 2.1.260, --model sonnet, --mcp-config with type http and the /t/<token> URL, --strict-mcp-config, no headers anywhere, per-tool allowlist of 61 mcp__<server>__<tool> entries built from a live tools/list (quotes 11, invoice 12, calendar 12, timezone 11, pdf 15), --output-format stream-json --verbose --max-turns 20, one --session-id then five --resume per lane. Per r11 D-R57 every lane ran in an EMPTY working directory with the CLI own filesystem tools disallowed (Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch, NotebookEdit); nothing shelled out. Fixtures sized under the base64 ceiling r11 D-R51 documented: two 1-page pdf-lib PDFs of 1009 and 1011 bytes (1348 characters of base64 each) and a 1272-byte .ics with 8 Europe/Warsaw events for the week of 2026-09-07. Tool-call counts exclude the client ToolSearch schema lookups. Machine day 2026-09-04.
rubric: 3 = correct, right numbers, no clarification. 2 = correct but needed a second turn, a workaround, or left the user a gap to close. 1 = partially wrong, or asked for something the tool could infer. 0 = failed.

defects.summary: The Pro refusal for ics_import {url} named the price and never the free paste path that gets the identical events. Hosted, path is refused by design and url is Pro, so paste is the only free way in, and this is the gate a free caller hits first. servers/calendar/src/index.ts now answers with the upgrade text plus a runnable ics_import {name, text} example carrying the name the caller already asked for. Test: D-R58: the url gate names the free text path that gets the same events.

pdf_split, pdf_rotate, pdf_stamp and pdf_reorder echo the input path back as source, and the link substitution only rewrites paths published in that request, so an input published by an EARLIER request printed raw as /out/invoices-merged.pdf - a virtual root the caller cannot see and not a string any tool accepts. remote/src/index.ts now gives pdf strip: [/uploads/, /out/], the same pair image and bank-statement already carry. Live: source invoices-merged.pdf.

Hosted business_set answers Business profile saved to /home/mcp/.local/share/mcp-servers/invoice and lists docx, expense-tracker, recurring, time-tracker, timezone, resume and clauses as the readers. The directory is the worker virtual homedir, and the list omits quotes, pdf and calendar, all three of which read that profile. The string lives in servers/invoice/src/index.ts, held by another agent this session. Fix direction: name the endpoint, not the path, and derive the reader list from the servers that import readSharedProfile.

event_export drops ATTENDEE lines. events_list shows the attendee and event_to_time_entry puts it in the note, but a round trip through export loses who was invited. Fix direction: carry ATTENDEE and ORGANIZER through icsText() the way LOCATION already is.

r11 D-R51 fixed what the upload tools say; it did not make the paste cheap. Two PDFs at 1348 characters of base64 each - roughly a seventieth of the 190 KB request-body ceiling - cost 76.4 s in one turn against 8.7 s for the next turn in the same session. The honest number for a hosted paste is tens of seconds for a couple of KB.

p4 answered a page count with no tool call, restating pdf_merge pages: 2 from the previous turn, after a stamp had rewritten the file in between. pdf_count exists and costs one call. Nothing server-side to fix; noted because it is the failure mode a scorecard cannot distinguish from a correct read.

insight: r11 seam was an endpoint stating a limit that is not the limit that binds. r12 is the same species one step down: an endpoint stating a PATH and a PRICE that are not the caller. pdf_stamp handed back /out/invoices-merged.pdf, a root with no meaning on the other side of a URL; ics_import answered the one gate a free hosted caller cannot route around with $19 and no mention of the paste that gets the identical events for nothing. The model recovered from both, which is exactly why neither showed up as a wrong answer.
